newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end higher but underperforms Dow.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end higher but underperforms Dow.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended higher on Wednesday, but a struggling gold sector kept the Canadian market from matching stronger gains in New York.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 17.44 points to close at 5727.64 in brisk turnover of nearly 95 million shares worth C$1.28 billion ($936 million).
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 38 points on the back of a hot technology sector.
In Toronto, gains in conglomerates, utilities and retailing were restrained by weak golds and a merger which sapped the paper products group.
The paper and forestry products group lost 41 points after Avenor Inc unveiled its proposed C$3.3 billion ($2.4 billion) acquisition of Repap Enterprises Inc.

"The gold sector was still struggling today...and the Avenor takeover of Repap did not meet with a whole lot of enthusiasm by the market," said Fred Ketchen, director of equity trading at ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
Toronto's advancing stocks edged past declines 478 to 470 with 322 issues unchanged.
* Avenor and Repap were among the TSE's heaviest traders.

Repap's stock fell 1.30 to 4.20 on 5.1 million shares, while Avenor dropped 1.80 to 19.40 on 2.8 million shares. Avenor said it planned to issue 29 million new shares as part of its all-stock offer for Repap.

* Canbra Foods Ltd. rebounded from Tuesday's selloff, climbing 3.25 to 18.25 on 92,000 shares. Canbra's stock sank on Tuesday after its majority shareholder withdrew an offer to buy the rest of the food company.
* Bre-X Minerals Ltd. and Barrick Gold Corp. remained active after agreeing to split the rich Busang gold find on Tuesday. Bre-X fell 0.25 to 7.65, while Barrick slipped 0.15 to 40.60.
